title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer priority-queue ordering to prevent regional failover thrashing
author: Jordan Patel
description:
Motivation: In production we observed moments of thrashing and unnecessary regional failovers during load spikes. The SLO enforcer's priority queue occasionally reordered requests deterministically in a way that starved higher-priority traffic and caused aggressive load-shedding + cross-region failover. Root cause: the comparator used for request ordering relied primarily on wall-clock enqueue time and a nondeterministic tie-breaker, which allowed bursty retries and region-penalty adjustments to flip ordering under high load. This resulted in priority inversion and cascading shed decisions across regions.

What this change does: 1) Fixes comparator to use a stable, multi-key priority: (request_priority, region_penalty, enqueue_time_ms, request_id) so higher-priority requests cannot be overtaken by retry bursts. 2) Adds backpressure smoothing: we now apply an exponential moving-average on recent shed rate per-region before triggering aggressive regional failover, to prevent rapid oscillation. 3) Introduces a feature flag (slo_enforcer.priority_stable_mode) and a configurable canary rollout (defaults to 10% of traffic/one region) for controlled rollout. 4) Adds unit and integration tests covering tie-breaking, ordering invariants, and simulated regional failover scenarios. 5) Improves metrics: new histogram slo_enforcer.queue_priority_depth and a shed_rate_smoothing gauge to help detect regressions.

Testing: - Unit tests for comparator and tie-breaker invariants added under services/slo-enforcer/test/priority_queue_test.go.
- Integration test simulating cross-region overload and verifying no more than one region flaps within 30s added under infra/tests/slo_enforcer_failover_integration.py (deterministic simulation harness).
- Local performance test run on staging loadbench (1000 rps over 10m) showed steady shed rates and eliminated thrashing seen in baseline.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag turned off. - Canary to region-us-west-2 at 10% traffic for 2h with close monitoring of sla.slo_error_rate and slo_enforcer.shed_rate (alert threshold: 15% increase over baseline). - If stable, graduate to 50% then global.

Rollback: - Disable slo_enforcer.priority_stable_mode via remote feature flag to revert to previous behaviour immediately.

Notes: This is a hotfix focused on correctness and stability rather than micro-optimizations (no change to batching semantics). Related Linear cards: ENG-4982 (stability), ENG-5021 (metrics/dashboards).
